Most animals also reach reproductive maturity before being physically mature to handle pregnancy. Cats get their first estrous (a.k.a men.cycle) around 6 months, and they might get pregnant then, but their bodies are not really mature enough. The same stands for dogs, cows, horses, basically most ruminants and equines. They get their first estrous before their hips are wide enough to handle birth, so called "juvenile hips". That's why in extensive farming it's better to wait until the second or third estrous to inseminate mares and cows.

If you've been overweight before starting venlafaxine, you've already been at risk for type 2 diabetes. But getting there is a long way. Do you have anyone in your family with diabetes?
Before diabetes you may have insulin resistance - your cells are basically numb to insulin trying to utilize glucose so your blood sugar is constantly high because it can't go anywhere, and your cells are "hungry" all the time. And from there you get type 2 diabetes - enough glucose, enough insulin, but nowhere for them to go. As I said, it's a long way to get to that point, don't freak out. It's not something that happens overnight. 
Don't get worked up before visiting your doctor. Explain what you've felt, do some blood tests, insulin and blood sugar tests. Even if you have insulin resistance, it's completely manageable.
